fixedQuestions: What should the character do? Why?

grain-we-keep: What if there were enough grain for everyone today, but no seed left for next year? Would your choice change? Why?
Does giving every household the same amount of grain make the decision fair? Why?
What would you need to know about the households before deciding how to share the grain?
grain-we-keep-animated: What if there were enough grain for everyone today, but no seed left for next year? Would your choice change? Why?
Does giving every household the same amount of grain make the decision fair? Why?
What would you need to know about the households before deciding how to share the grain?
measure-that-changed-ethics: What if the person asking for extra grain were a stranger rather than a friend? Would your choice change? Why?
Can giving different amounts of grain to different households be fair? Why?
Which matters more here: following the agreed rule or meeting an urgent need? Why?
price-of-peace-ethics: What if returning Aruna would put him in danger? Would your advice change? Why?
Can an agreement between rulers be fair if the people affected have no say? Why?
What would you need to know before advising whether Aruna should be returned?
dinner-with-the-tyrant: What if accepting the meal meant promising never to criticise the ruler? Would your choice change? Why?
Can someone accept a ruler’s help and still be independent? Why?
Which matters more here: staying free from the ruler or gaining a chance to help someone? Why?
one-more-step-toward-peace: What if helping one patient put the other patients at greater risk? Would your choice change? Why?
Can caring for one person conflict with caring for a whole hospital? Explain using the episode.
What would you need to know before deciding how much risk the hospital should take?
courage-without-applause: What if nobody would ever know who helped with the rescue? Would your choice change? Why?
Can someone feel afraid and still be brave? Explain using the rescue.
If a risky rescue succeeds through luck, does that make it a wise choice? Why?
the-welcome-nobody-wanted: What would make stepping back from the welcome become neglect? Explain using the canopy incident.
What if the official would never know who helped? Would Lan’s choices still show care? Why?
Which matters more in this welcome: keeping a shared ritual or returning people’s time? Why?
the-sheep-behind-our-house: Can Jun refuse his father’s request and still show filial care? Explain why.
What if the sheep’s owner were a stranger to Jun? Would his responsibility change? Why?
Does returning the sheep repair all the harm? What else should count, and why?
